page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 1890 GB of local disk capacity and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

The underlying x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong performance in specific workloads. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 36.5 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 15.18 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong at 231.56 GB/sec. PassMark CPU tests yield a strong score of 54563.93, with notable performance in encryption and physics simulations.

Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small-block cached bandwidth of 2684.62 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write speeds reach 166.74 GB/sec and 65.26 GB/sec respectively. The instance delivers a static web serving throughput of 59.6 GB/sec and handles 61.6 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. For machine learning tasks, the server achieves a strong prompt processing speed of 3133.77 tokens/sec on small LLM models. This hardware profile is suited for general-purpose workloads, relational databases, web serving, and moderate data processing tasks requiring local NVMe storage.
